answer: A synchronous ceremony admits twenty seats through a harbor registry, answering the same questions live. Each seat records one fingerprint, and fingerprints too close on a trellis are clustered and flagged. A yarrow seal binds each fingerprint to its seat, and a copied seal fails the match. Each seat requires a 60 credit bond, locked until closing and returned after a ceremony. The k-th fake needs a k-th human, fingerprint, and bond, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 people and 60,000 credits. Hired stand-ins fail: one fingerprint binds to one seat.
